task.title: Refer to tasks by title, not ID, when communicating with humans
task.description:
The workbook skill correctly drills agents on resolving and reusing the canonical full task ID for every CLI command, but agents mirror that habit into their prose: status updates, summaries, and questions to the user say things like "finished WB-01KYD730XZ9S88N1GGGSSG2CJ5" — a ULID a human cannot parse, remember, or distinguish from any other. IDs are the machine interface; titles are the human interface.

Update the skill source (skills/workbook/SKILL.md, the source generated into .claude/skills/workbook) to make the distinction explicit: an agent reads, selects, and mutates tasks by full ID, but when communicating with a human it leads with the task title (e.g. "Add remote claim and lease workflow"), mentioning the ID only when it adds value — disambiguating similarly titled tasks, or when the human needs to run a command themselves.

Acceptance criteria:
- The skill instructs agents to use the resolved full ID for every workbook CLI invocation (unchanged behavior).
- The skill instructs agents to refer to tasks by title in all human-facing communication: progress reports, completion summaries, questions, and error reports.
- The guidance covers the common surfaces where IDs currently leak: announcing which task was selected, reporting lifecycle transitions, and describing dependencies or blockers.
- The regenerated .claude/skills/workbook copy reflects the change (regenerate via the repo's skill generation workflow rather than editing the generated copy).
- An agent following the updated skill, asked to take the next task, announces it by title.
